authorization.scope: mysql-repository.ts transaction-end connection disposal, its two tests, docs/slide/development/MAX-237/**; no public contract, DDL, shared pool, route, runtime, frontend, migration or consumer change

defect.summary: A failed/unknown transaction end was released back to the pool. MySQL implicitly commits an open transaction at the next START TRANSACTION on that connection, so a later unrelated write could persist the failed operation's rows.
defect.pre_fix_evidence: t2a-tx-cleanup-probe-pre-fix.json (replays the Chief counterexamples; both fail with released_to_pool=1 and independent_after_unrelated_create={parents:1,drafts:0|1})

fix.rule: release only after a confirmed commit or a confirmed rollback; destroy otherwise (unconfirmed rollback, lost commit acknowledgement, failed begin, failed session setup)
fix.interface: TemplateSqlConnection gained the explicit destroy(): void slice (adapter-local type; no public schema/export of product contracts)
fix.error_semantics: the original operation error is preserved when rollback is unconfirmed; commit uncertainty stays TEMPLATE_STORAGE_UNKNOWN_COMMIT with the same redacted identity and is re-read read-only on a new connection; no automatic retry
fix.discard_failure: a throwing destroy() is swallowed so it can never replace the operation outcome, and the connection is never released instead
